title: Canonical comparisons for composition of smooth purity maps
statement:
Work at the finite coefficient stage $A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$, of
[def-pur-conventions], on the small pro-etale derived categories. Use the
pullback and tensor of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the prescribed
Tate twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and the shift reassociation
appearing in [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. For a $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ and
$d\geq0$, write $T_f^d(K)=(Lf^*K)(d)[2d]$.

Define the canonical comparisons as follows. Ordered nonnegative shifted Tate
tensor powers are concatenated recursively using the tensor unit at exponent
zero, the successor tensor product, and the tensor associator. The symmetry
reverses the two blocks to the order $e,d$, with the derived Koszul sign.
Tate pullback is the restriction-of-roots comparison followed by comparison
of the etale and pro-etale sites. Tensor pullback is the derived monoidal
pullback comparison transported along the exact inverse-image comparison;
pullback composition is the derived exact upper-star compositor. All scalar
coordinate changes use the canonical constant-ring realization equivalences.

For composable $k$-morphisms $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$, $d,e\geq0$, and
$K\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, define
$$a_{f,g,d,e,K}:T_{gf}^{d+e}(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_f^d(T_g^e(K))$$
by these eight factors in order: shift reassociation for $d+e$; pullback
composition tensored with the ordered Tate-power splitting; inverse tensor
associator; inverse Tate pullback in the $e$ factor; inverse tensor-pullback
comparison; inverse shift reassociation for $d$; the shifted pullback of
inverse shift reassociation for $e$; and insertion of the realization unit
at $Y$. The full isomorphism, including its inverse, is uniquely characterized
by equality of every factor with these specified canonical factors and equality
with their composite. Thus no arbitrary endpoint isomorphism is chosen.

For separated finite-type $k$-morphisms $f,g$ of finite-type $k$-schemes,
let $E_f=Rf^!$ be the standing exceptional inverse image of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], in intrinsic constant-ring coordinates.
For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ define
$$c_{g,f,K}:E_{gf}K\xrightarrow{\sim}E_fE_gK$$
to be the standing counit mate of [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition],
transported through those realization equivalences, with the realization unit
inserted at $Y$. Its inverse is the unique inverse of that specified mate.
For smooth $g$ of pure relative dimension $e\geq0$, $E_gK$ is in
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, so the second purity map in the composition formula is typed.
No separatedness over $k$ is required of the schemes themselves. These definitions
fix the comparison maps only; equality of the smooth purity maps under them
is a separate theorem.
